claim: Replace the BCM4389 versioned join request's deprecated one-element array without changing its firmware wire layout or truncating the optional channel allocation.
oracle: Actual-C tests preserve 76/78-byte wire requests and all field offsets, cover allocation and firmware errors, and detect the header-only under-allocation mutation under ASan. Exact-kernel W=1 build passes.

user_journey.scenario: User selects Wi-Fi with or without a fixed channel; request reaches firmware with the same correct bytes, and allocation/firmware errors return cleanly.
user_journey.expected: No association regression or heap overflow introduced by the flexible-array cleanup; hardware association remains a separate test.

invariants: Only versioned BCM4389 join structure and its allocation change
All allocation sizes derive from the existing wire-length calculation
No change to legacy join or radio power
All references to the two versioned structs audited
gitnexus: External pinned source; direct call-site search used instead of an unavailable graph
ast: Compile extracted actual structs and join function with mocked allocation and firmware boundary

unit.red: Changing only array[1] to array[] while retaining sizeof allocation must trigger ASan on channel-present case
unit.green: Length-based allocation passes golden byte-layout tests, absent/present BSSID, channel, empty/max SSID, allocation failure and firmware rejection
cases: no firmware call on allocation failure

evidence: Pinned W2 source uses chanspec_list[1] and kzalloc_obj(*jp); blindly converting the array reduces sizeof and would lose space for one channel.
limitations: No radio load or association in this offline stage
Golden layout is based on existing working protocol source, not independent firmware reverse engineering
W3 still requires authorized network and DMA/recovery plan
exit_gate: Actual-C RED/GREEN and unchanged wire layout, warning-free kernel build and scoped checkpatch before any W3 driver load.
status: Actual-code RED/GREEN and exact-kernel W=1 build passed; no phone driver trial or association.
